entries.finding: The X-facing upper brick panels rendered without physical arched openings.
entries.fix: Replaced the orientation-sensitive profile Boolean with explicit rectangular and circular crown cutters, then rerendered both side envelopes.

entries.finding: Lantern end faces were visually open and could not prove a closed weathering enclosure.
entries.fix: Added glazed gable-end polygons and seated iron end frames to both axes of the source-locked T lantern.

entries.finding: The registered printing rosette plane was inside the physical carrier thickness and therefore invisible.
entries.fix: Registered the derivative to the carrier's audited exterior face rather than its center datum.

entries.finding: The upper occupied-depth layer initially read as a flat opaque brown card.
entries.fix: Made the room layer restrained and translucent while retaining a separate setback, room sidewalls, warm illumination, and visible furnishings.

entries.finding: The first side camera cropped the parapet extremities.
entries.fix: Moved both orthogonal side cameras outward and rerendered grade-to-parapet with neutral margin.

entries.finding: Overlapping lantern sheds produced protruding rods, crossing members, and discontinuous curb ownership.
entries.fix: Rebuilt one joined T envelope with a continuous outline, closed vertical faces, mitered central facets, bounded ridges/ribs, and one flashing owner.

entries.finding: Corner posts, railing, cornice, and corbel cadence were generic or oversized.
entries.fix: Used lobed brick corner profiles, finer lower diamond ironwork, a thinner cornice, and dense small brackets.

entries.finding: Bright stone formed invented continuous plinth, sill, cap, and lantern ribbons.
entries.fix: Restored dark steel/brick ownership and limited warm-gray stone to structural foot and support roles.

entries.finding: Brick stretched across curves and was too coarse/orange.
entries.fix: Applied reference-conditioned world tri-planar mapping with corrected course scale and restrained saturation.

entries.finding: Glazing and iron were too dark/noisy for consistent optical proof.
entries.fix: Raised neutral exposure, increased pane transmission, softened iron values, and preserved separate occupied depth.

entries.finding: The interior read as generic workshop furniture rather than a legible printing workflow.
entries.fix: Added and separated complete platen presses, type/paper storage, feed beds, rollers, and flywheels behind primary glazing.

entries.finding: The T lantern remained shallow, had open/free frame ends, ambiguous crossing members, weak flashing proof, and an invalid exterior below camera.
entries.fix: Built a taller closed monitor over a full-depth T roof aperture, added closed end frames, interior returns and rectangular flashing laps, removed redundant valley rods, and re-authored an interior-up daylight view.

entries.finding: Corner finials and the under-cornice bracket rhythm remained simplified.
entries.fix: Replaced round finials with stepped/notched crossed brick profiles and doubled the seated stem-and-head corbel cadence.

entries.finding: The rosette baked a second orange brick family over a washed envelope brick.
entries.fix: Restricted the registered derivative to the iron rosette and restored one darker tawny tri-planar envelope brick authority.

entries.finding: The roof material read as a clean modular panel grid.
entries.fix: Generated and mapped an exact-source-conditioned aged bituminous membrane with broad irregular patches and laps at whole-roof scale.

entries.finding: Dither noise and obstructed proof suppressed the optical section and printing program.
entries.fix: Used blended pane/occupied layers, balanced a source-consistent press proof light, and re-authored the close camera through a clear pane.

entries.finding: The T-monitor still read as overlapping roofs; bounded joints, continuous weathering ownership, and a full-depth interior aperture were not proven.
entries.fix: Rebuilt the monitor as one shared-vertex glazed envelope with a joined flashing skirt, joined curb/roof return, bounded square frame members, explicit valley members, and a resolved central node; widened the occupied-interior proof camera.

entries.finding: Aerial and rear-side cameras clipped the visible footprint/base.
entries.fix: Pulled both cameras back and raised their framing to retain grade, roof peak, full footprint, and neutral margin.

entries.finding: The rosette was oversized, corner finials were stepped ziggurats, and detached cuboid corbels did not support the cornice.
entries.fix: Reduced the iron-only rosette/carrier, authored compact lobed brick finials, and replaced the corbels with shaped seated brackets that overlap the cornice datum.

entries.finding: Facade mullions and glare obstructed the printing press evidence.
entries.fix: Moved the proof cameras inside the occupied room, reduced the proof light, and framed the complete press and surrounding workflow without facade obstruction.

entries.finding: Monitor facets split into dark perforated and opaque white surface families, preventing one sealed aged-glass reading at the T node.
entries.fix: Assigned one exact-source-calibrated translucent aged-monitor material to every vertical, end, valley, and sloped facet while retaining the joined curb, flashing, gaskets, bounded bars, and explicit T node.

entries.finding: Front-corner and aerial cameras crowded or clipped the closest base/footprint.
entries.fix: Pulled both cameras back and raised the target margin to contain grade-to-monitor and the complete visible footprint.

entries.finding: Corner finials remained low rounded stumps and cornice brackets remained too blocky.
entries.fix: Rebuilt taller faceted pointed brick pinnacles from the locked oblique silhouette and replaced the bracket band with a finer cadence of slender tapered supports seated into the cornice.

entries.finding: Cornice brackets were seated but still read as flat triangular teeth rather than projecting source consoles.
entries.fix: Rebuilt every support as a narrow 3D console with lower wall seat, narrowed neck, projecting head, and positive contact at the cornice underside on front, rear, and sides.

entries.finding: Coarse large-X railing and one repeated symmetric rosette crest genericized the roof-edge identity.
entries.fix: Rebuilt fine two-tier diamond lattice with thinner members; differentiated all visible crest profiles and added bounded triangular shoulder reliefs from the locked front, oblique, and top sources.
